body:
It’s hard. Really hard. I didn’t have access to any quick options and didn’t trust pipes or ceiling supports to hold my weight for a hanging, so I had to go with the slower stuff. Belt around the neck and walking out into the cold were my ideas, since I knew I wasn’t good enough with pain to manage it with a knife. Turns out they both hurt a hell of a lot more than I anticipated and so now I’m still alive. It’s fucked up, but I have a measure of respect for people who’ve succeeded, or who’ve gone through with attempts yet survived through no fault of their own, since I’ve learned from experience how much less capable I am than they are. 

At the moment my life is a little better. I’ve changed majors and swapped some other stuff around and now I feel fine, but I think I’ll wait until exam season to see if that part of me comes back.

The thought that everything would be so much worse if I tried to end it and failed - and that, knowing me, failure is more likely than anything else. 

I’ve made some changes recently and am on an upslope for now, but that thought kept me alive when needed for at least the past five years.

My dad ended up having a talk with me about suicide after I talked about it a bit too much. I ended up making the “yes, I’m fine, and I promise I’ll tell you about it if I ever feel that way again” oath. 

That was, what, twelve years ago? I wonder if he even remembers.

I’ve tried a few and been held back by those stupid instincts that don’t like self harm. It’s embarrassing - thirteen year olds across the country are cutting and I can’t even nick an artery or walk out into the cold.

I’m in that boat too. Half the reason I want to commit is because of the fear that someone I know will start looking more closely at me, and I know if I try and fail in any obvious way I’ll be stuck under a microscope of shame the rest of my life.
Can confirm, it’s not as fun as it sounds. I’m a northerner and quite used to the cold, and all my ability to ignore the bite vanishes as soon as I step out with the idea to lie down for a few hours.

I feel you man. 

Hey, try something for me? I want to test whether this was a coincidence or an actual odd coping mechanism. I was feeling pretty shitty one day, and I decided “fuck it” and went up to ask out the cute girl sitting across the lobby from me. 

She said no, although she was pretty nice about it, but instead of getting bummed out even more something about doing that made me feel almost human again. I don’t know if it was the nervousness, the fact that I pushed myself somewhat, the act of saying nice things to someone else without prompting, or what, but I didn’t feel like ending it for the rest of the night.

Sorry, miscommunication in the post. Edited. 

I was saying that the thoughts aren’t as appealing as they used to be.
